b: This day is a sweet day.. The day I part from them for the first time and travel by bus alone.. Before that, let me finish telling the story of what we went round and saw

The first place we went was an abandoned water park.. Apparently someone who wanders about like us discovered it.. People had forgotten there was even a water park like this… If someone had discovered Athipatti like this, Ajith wouldn't have had to become a Citizen

Though the government set out to demolish it as an unsafe place, the local people won't let them and are protecting it now.. When we went in, a man took money saying it was needed to protect the place.. Actually there's no such ticket.. And it wasn't that clean inside either.. No use arguing, so we paid..

Inside there was a huge dragon with its mouth open, enormous.. That's what everyone comes to see..Inside, bat droppings everywhere.. We went in carefully without touching anything.. Like our people, they've scribbled all over the walls.. Lots of lovers, thinking it's a tomb, have carved their names.. How many of them are still going round as couples, only the dragon knows

When we came out after looking around everything, we were really thirsty.. Outside, as if he knew, the man who'd taken the money was standing with bottles of water and soda.. No choice! We bought water and drank it right there.. Then he asked which country we were from.. We said Sri Lanka.. He didn't know it .. Then he said he collects the money of the countries people come from.. Before we could think he was taking money from us again, Mithra handed him our fifty rupees.. When we asked, it was to spread the country's glory, apparently… If he goes to change that money, he'll speak very gloriously of us…

After that we went to see a tomb.. The ticket price was in lakhs… We can't pay all that, we said, bought ice cream at the shop next door and ate it..After finishing that we set off to see the palace (since there are girls here prettier than in Sundar C's films, everywhere we looked was a palace)

People who watch Korean serials would have liked the palace we went to.. Pretty much like those, a big palace in Chinese-Mongolian architecture..It took a long time to look around inside … with gardens and wells, the maharajas seem to have lived very well indeed.. But in the pictures none of them was very good-looking .. They looked ordinary, pot bellies and all, like us.. It's these serials that make them good-looking and send everyone mad, boys and girls alike..

After that we went to the rooms .. We had to go to the next town by bus.. 12 hours… Since I'd joined late, I couldn't get a ticket on theirs.. So I had to take another bus… So I had to go alone.. I didn't tell my family.. If they'd known, Amma would have clutched her chest and collapsed.. Even in Colombo, if I go alone I get lost.. Once like this, coming home from the temple, I took a new route … and got lost.. Then I caught an auto and somehow got back..

In this state, on some blind courage, I set off alone.. These guys sent me off saying I need to learn all this.. When I went and stood at the bus stand, there were lots of buses.. Like our Jaffna buses.. When I showed my ticket and asked each person, they pointed and told me to wait.. In the end a bus came and they told me to get on it.. As I got on, afraid I was getting into who knows what and going who knows where, the conductor had a ticket with my name written on it.. Only after seeing that did I feel at peace..

This is a sleeper bus .. The seats were like bunk beds.. They told us to take off our shoes and put them in a shopping bag and sent us in.. Window seat .. you can lie back in comfort.. There was room to stretch your legs too.. We should bring these to our part of the world too.. Only I know the suffering of not being able to stretch your legs on a sitting bus

Once they'd made sure I was on the bus, they got on their bus too.. We'd arrive at about the same time.. We set off planning to meet there.. I slept well, and when I woke in the morning the bus had started going in the opposite direction from where I had to get off .. And there was no one else on the bus .. From Kathirgama Kandan on, there was no god I didn't pray to.. Afraid of which forest he'd drop me in, I went to talk to the driver and he didn't even turn round… Well, that's the full stop to the Vietnam story, I thought, and he braked..
With this, the stories of southern Vietnam come to an end.. The visit to the north will continue next season.. For now a short break.. for me and for you
note: "Journeys Never End" (Payanangal Mudivathillai, 1982) is a Tamil film title. In the film Citizen (2001), the actor Ajith plays a man whose village, Athipatti, was wiped off the map. Sundar C directs the Aranmanai ("Palace") horror-comedy films. Kathirgama Kandan is Murugan of Kataragama.
